text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a small cluster of tenants with double-counted tokens in invoice_preview for short-lived sessions (100–300ms).
lin: :eyes: any common filter? route, model, sampling?
maria: All on the new microburst routing policy we rolled yesterday (route-priority v2). Mostly text-generation, high concurrency with rapid connect/disconnect.
jamal: Do we have an example event trace?
maria: Pasted one I pulled from debug logs: ```
{"tenant":"T-846","session_id":"s-9a3","events":[{"type":"req_start","ts":1718885000},{"type":"req_end","ts":1718885001},{"type":"req_start","ts":1718885002},{"type":"req_end","ts":1718885003}],"route":"microburst-v2","tokens": [12,12] }
```
maria: The ledger is counting both req pairs as separate billing items instead of collapsing to a single session token tally.
sre_alex: Hmm, looks like the session boundary detector is keyed on connection_id but LB does short-lived rehandshakes that change connection_id mid-session. That would break dedupe.
lin: We added connection_id fallback to peer_ip when canarying microburst. Maybe fallback logic is too permissive and splits session when balancing moves.
jamal: Could be the routing proxy rewriting x-tenant-session header during a fast failover. I've seen that with the new sticky-handoff path.
ops-bot: ALERT: invoice_preview drift anomaly detected — 13 tenants > 2% variance vs last 24h baseline (alert id 9b3f).
billing-bot: sample invoice diff: tenant T-846 preview shows +24 tokens vs expected after route-priority canary.
sre_alex: Quick mitigation: revert microburst fallback to use stable session_fingerprint (hash of tenant+user_agent+session_start) instead of connection_id/peer_ip. That avoids splits when LB changes conn ids.
lin: Agree. Can we gate that behind a feature flag and do a canary for 5% of traffic?
maria: Yes — we'll flip feature flag for canary, add a temporary aggregator in the preview pipeline to coalesce events within 1s for the same fingerprint.
jamal: Also add an alert for sudden upticks in "invoice_preview_diff_per_tenant" to catch regressions before full rollout.
sre_alex: I'll open a short-lived runbook for rollback: revert flag, clear preview aggregator state, and kick a lightweight backfill for affected tenants.
maria: Plan timeline: flag deploy in 30m, canary 5% for 1h, monitor billing-bot diffs and console metric invoice_preview_var. If good, ramp to 100% over 2h.
lin: Small ask — add a dashboard card showing "session_fingerprint_collisions" and "connection_id_changes_per_session" so we can see root cause during canary.
maria: Will add. Also adding a one-off query to find tenants with >3 splits per minute and queueing them for manual review.
jamal: Sounds good. Thanks — ping me if you need help with proxy rules.
sre_alex: On it. :thumbsup:
maria: filing postmortem checklist now in #postmortems (will include the event schema snippet and the rollback steps).
